name: Fraud and risk analyst
oneLine: Signals, scores, chargebacks, agent abuse patterns.
goals: Tell agent-initiated transactions apart from human and bot traffic in the data the model sees.
Build features from agent identity, mandate constraints and payment tokens that predict disputes.
Catch new abuse patterns: agent farms, prompt-injected purchases, mandate stretching, replayed credentials.
Keep approval rates high for legitimate agents while dispute rates stay flat.
Feed risk signals back into the protocol fields that carry them (ACP risk signals, AP2 risk_data, Agent Score).
pains: Agent indicators are missing or unreliable in authorization data, and the networks are testing probability scores instead.
Agents that fill card forms with token-shaped values look like card testing in rules built for humans.
Velocity rules break: one agent can legitimately make hundreds of small payments a minute on x402 or MPP.
Sybil reputations on ERC-8004 (59.2% to 90.6% of reviewers flagged on three chains in arXiv:2606.26028, data to 2026-05-13) and farmed x402 volume make external trust signals noisy.
No public agent-specific dispute reason codes exist (Mastercard's Agent Pay Program Standards are not public), so chargeback labels do not tell the analyst what went wrong.
A compromised agent can run within its mandate and still cause harm, so limit checks alone are not enough.
decisions: Which agent-related features enter the risk model and how to weight unverified ones.
Rule changes for agent traffic: velocity, device, geolocation and merchant-category exceptions.
Review and step-up thresholds for agent-initiated orders.
Which external trust signals (registries, scores, trusted lists) are allowed into decisions.
